difficulties: None blocking. The benchmark drivers are mechanism-generic (CSV columns and output come from the generated descriptor), so swapping configs/ts1.json was enough; the Makefile has no variable for the configuration path. One caveat for reading the protocol's results: make bench generates kernels for a fixed width of 32 cells (SPECIALIZE_WIDTH defaults to GROUP_SIZE) with generic fallbacks for any other width, so on the 4-cell problem the specialized program ran the generic kernels inside the generated Rosenbrock instantiation, and its specialized_vs_generic is bit-identical by construction. The generated kernels were exercised in a supplementary build with SPECIALIZE_WIDTH=4 (a documented Makefile variable, no entry change): all PASS against generic and MICM. The addendum run on 64 distinct cells (two full 32-cell groups) with the default build does use the generated kernels (probe: zero fallback calls) and passes everywhere. The converter omits per-species molecular weights (absent from canonical.json; the reader needs them only for SURFACE reactions). make env downloaded about 25 MB of conda-forge packages into the worktree's own package cache (the Makefile sets CONDA_PKGS_DIRS to .conda-pkgs), so the setup used the network once.
generated_kernels_evidence: Code path: src/bench.c:26 sets group_size = CHEM_GROUP_SIZE (32, from GROUP_SIZE); lines 42-46 cap it at cells/threads unless --group-size is given; line 47 caps it at cells. With --threads 1: 4 cells -> one 4-cell group; 64 cells -> two 32-cell groups. The default build generates with --fixed-width 32, and each of the six generated kernels branches on the group width: sp_forcing "if (s->cells != 32) { chem_forcing(s, y, f); return; }", likewise sp_jacobian -> chem_negative_jacobian, sp_alpha -> chem_alpha_minus_jacobian, sp_factor -> chem_factor, sp_backsolve -> chem_linear_solve, ts1_update_rates -> chem_update_rates. Only the generated Rosenbrock loop (fused stages, SIMD error norm) runs in both cases. Runtime check (no debugger: macOS developer mode is off): probe/ compiles the unmodified build/ts1_specialized.c with a forced-include header renaming those six fallback calls to counting wrappers, links it like bin/ts1_bench_specialized, and reproduces its output byte for byte. Counts: at 4 cells every call falls back (forcing 1098, jacobian 549, alpha 549, factor 549, solve 1647, rates 1); at 64 cells none do (all 0), for all three mechanisms.
